mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% over three consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower (t-test p > 0.10) when this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) falling below 3.5% for two consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings for industrial firms and drags down S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly different from zero when INDPRO declines persist.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in FEDFUNDS and a decline in CPIAUCSL (core inflation) below 2.5% over two months signals a disinflationary tightening, which raises real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS growth > 0.4% monthly for two months) and housing starts (HOUST) above their 12-month moving average signals a demand expansion, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 0.4% for 2 months AND HOUST > 12-mo MA for 2 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly above zero in more than 70% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the unemployment rate above 4.5% for four consecutive months, combined with a decline in payrolls (PAYEMS), signals deteriorating labor market conditions and reduced consumer spending power, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 4.5% for 4 consecutive months AND PAYEMS monthly change < 0%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both triggers are met.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annualized GDP growth (GDPC1) above 4% for two consecutive quarters signals a robust demand environment, which supports corporate earnings and justifies higher equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly above zero when GDP growth exceeds 4% for two quarters.
